info.title: Hangang Management API
info.description:
Authenticated configuration and observation API. Route mutations are atomic and require the quoted current revision in If-Match. Dynamic Docker references use this instance's administrator-managed Docker connection or an initial CLI socket.

Management accounts are local to each instance. Viewer sessions may read runtime and update status plus health and metrics; configuration and user operations require administrator role. The existing administrator bearer token remains available for break-glass access.

get.summary: Read local collector observations (administrator only)
get.description: Returns a copied local, partial snapshot without waiting on peers. Available means the inventory is valid; fresh_nodes counts fresh responses regardless of peer readiness. Stale or failed samples never imply current readiness. Requires live administrator authority. Cache-Control: no-store.

get.summary: Read one local node observation with its dedicated observer bearer token
get.description: Uses only the private observer credential, never an administrator session. No peer polling. Duplicate Authorization headers and query strings are rejected. Cache-Control: no-store.

get.summary: Read local observer credential readiness (administrator only)
get.description: Requires live administrator authority. Disabled mode reports configured=false, available=false, node_id=null, generation=null. Cache-Control: no-store.

get.summary: Read node-local country database readiness (administrator only)
get.description: Instance-local observation; no filesystem paths or MMDB contents. Requires live administrator authority after reading. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Country is approximate address metadata, not authenticated identity.

get.summary: Look up a country using the node-local database (administrator only)
get.description: Instance-local observation; no filesystem paths or MMDB contents. Requires live administrator authority after reading. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Country is approximate address metadata, not authenticated identity.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Exactly one IPv4 or IPv6 address; mapped IPv4 canonicalizes. No other parameters accepted.

get.summary: Export retained V2 SQL receipts in bounded snapshot-prefix pages
get.description: Administrator-only no-store per-authority sequence-ordered pages. First page pins a high-water and retention generation. New commits above that high-water do not change the exported prefix. Generation mismatch or high-water regression returns 409; restart export and discard partial data. Final empty probe with the same snapshot can recheck the retention fence. This is retained SQL commit evidence, not all accepted operations, archive durability, activation or fleet acknowledgement. Unknown and duplicate query parameters are rejected. Live authority is rechecked after storage I/O.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Exclusive cursor; defaults to zero. Nonzero requires both snapshot fields. Canonical decimal without sign or leading zeros.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; defaults to 100. Canonical decimal without sign or leading zeros.

parameters.name: snapshot_high_water
parameters.description: Pinned prefix high-water; supply together with retention_generation. Canonical decimal without sign or leading zeros.

parameters.name: retention_generation
parameters.description: Pinned retention generation; supply together with snapshot_high_water. Canonical decimal without sign or leading zeros.

200.description: Pinned retained receipt page or unsupported store

get.summary: Look up a sequenced V2 SQL commit receipt
get.description: Administrator-only no-store historical receipt in the authority/acceptance-sequence namespace. Separate from legacy random-ID lookup. Reports committed sequence and bounded authority registry; absent receipt does not prove non-commit. No pruning or replay. Live authority rechecked after remote read.

parameters.name: acceptance_seq
parameters.description: Canonical decimal without leading zero or sign.

get.summary: Look up a retained SQL configuration commit receipt
get.description: Administrator-only no-store historical commit evidence. Neither current configuration nor local activation nor fleet acknowledgement. Both identifiers are required exactly once; unknown query parameters rejected. File and Redis are unsupported. Absence is not non-commit evidence. Live account authority is rechecked after the external read. Ledger capacity is finite with no pruning in this phase; safe retention requires durable replay fencing.

get.summary: Read current configuration authority operation proof
get.description: Administrator-only current-row observation. SQLite and PostgreSQL support operation-aware CAS; File and Redis are unsupported. Null proof does not establish that an earlier operation never committed. This is neither local activation nor fleet acknowledgement nor historical audit. No query parameters. Live account authority is rechecked after the external read.

post.summary: Release one locally completed V2 SQL receipt pin
post.description: Administrator-only explicit recovery. The local operation must be V2 and candidate_activated, and its exact retained SQL receipt must match authority, acceptance sequence, operation ID, candidate digest, epoch and revision. A durable release identity makes a lost acknowledgement recoverable. This does not delete a SQL receipt, archive it, or prove fleet activation. An unknown outcome must be refreshed and must not be automatically retried by the client.

Administrator-only irreversible retention change. Preserves accepted and indeterminate records. Exact latest sequence and history revision are required; acceptance, completion or another prune invalidates stale decisions. Deletion and an account-audit config_operations_prune receipt commit atomically; audit capacity/failure rolls back deletion. Caller must archive required evidence; the server does not verify an archive.

200.description: Pruned terminal records and durable retention audit receipt; no-store

get.summary: List locally accepted configuration operations
get.description: Administrator-only durable acceptance and local outcome observations for HTTP configuration writes. Accepted operations may finish after logout. Candidate activation is an instance observation, not a unique remote writer proof or a fleet acknowledgement. Unresolved accepted/indeterminate rows are retained; no automatic replay. Explicit guarded pruning can remove archived terminal rows.

get.summary: Download this public API description
Check the authenticated admin listener
Read Prometheus metrics
get.description: Includes route Lua policy capacity, native JWT authentication, inbound TCP mutual-TLS, dedicated HTTP mutual-TLS, and workload route authorization counters. Listener handshake/generation rejection, listener lease termination, route identity denial, and route stream termination are separate counters.

get.summary: Read cache configuration, capacity and counters

post.summary: Purge memory and disk cache entries
post.description: File and controller modes: advances the runtime cache epoch before clearing local storage so an older in-flight fill cannot republish an entry after the purge. Shared-store mode: raises `cache.generation` in the shared configuration through a compare-and-swap, so every instance purges when it activates the new revision; the response carries the new revision and `ETag`.

200.description: Cache purged, or caching is disabled

get.summary: Stream live aggregate status and bounded connection metadata
get.description: Bearer-authenticated SSE. The first `event: status` frame arrives immediately and subsequent status frames about once per second; each `data:` line contains the same JSON object as GET /v1/status. Admins additionally receive bounded `event: traffic` frames containing TrafficBatch deltas and `event: tcp_connections` frames containing {active:TcpActiveBatch,recent:TcpRecentBatch} on every tick, including empty snapshots so the final active or untracked connection clears. Recent starts after the latest event ID at subscription. Viewers never receive IP-bearing traffic or TCP connection events. Account sessions are revalidated each tick; revocation yields `event: auth_expired` with `{}` and closes. Use a streaming fetch with the Authorization header; query-string tokens and all query parameters are rejected. At most 32 active event streams per instance. Frames are demand-driven and the stream permit is released on disconnect.

200.description: Server-sent events (status, admin-only traffic/TCP connections, or auth_expired)

get.summary: Read bounded active TCP connection metadata (administrator only)
get.description: Instance-local, best-effort active inventory in accept-ID order. A record can start or end between pages. IDs and byte counts are decimal strings to retain JavaScript precision. Includes peer IP, selected route/member, country observation and completed write bytes; no payload, credentials, filesystem path or raw error. Live administrator authority is rechecked after reading. Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return active connection IDs greater than this canonical unsigned decimal cursor. Omit or use 0 to start at the oldest tracked active record; server rejects values above u64.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Canonical decimal 1..128; duplicate, unknown and malformed parameters are rejected.

get.summary: Read bounded recently completed TCP connection metadata (administrator only)
get.description: Instance-local completion-event history retained up to 60 seconds or 4096 records; gaps and dropped/omitted counts are explicit. Completion order is independent of accept order. IDs, cursors, byte and cumulative counts are decimal strings. No payload, credentials, filesystem path or raw error. Live administrator authority is rechecked after reading. Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return completion event IDs greater than this canonical unsigned decimal cursor; omit for latest records. Server rejects values above u64.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Canonical decimal 1..128; duplicate, unknown and malformed parameters are rejected.

get.summary: Read recent bounded HTTP request metadata (administrator only)
get.description: Returns no request or response bodies, headers, cookies, authorization values, or query strings. Records describe response heads, not body completion. Ring retention is 60 seconds or 4096 records, whichever evicts first; `gap` and `dropped_total` expose retention loss. Cursor IDs are monotonic per process instance.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return records with IDs greater than this process-local cursor. Omit for the most recent records.

get.summary: Read this instance's configured public certificate metadata and observed ACME status (administrator only)
get.description: Paginated public leaf-certificate metadata from configured files. Omitted listener_id or default selects the legacy public listener; a named ID selects only that listener, including disabled definitions. Named inventories never inherit in-process ACME status. No private keys, PEM, file paths, account identifiers or raw ACME errors are returned. A configured binding is not proof that the current file bytes are in the live TLS resolver; the watcher can retain a previous valid generation. Standalone ACME attribution requires an explicitly configured private issuer status manifest with matching domains, expiry and leaf DER SHA-256. This is instance-local and does not control another gateway's certificates. Manual CLI TLS and Kubernetes TLS are outside this file inventory.

parameters.name: listener_id
parameters.description: Named public listener ID, or default for the legacy public listener. Unknown IDs return 404.

get.summary: Read this instance's configured backend targets and live selection state (administrator only)
get.description: Paginated from the current configuration snapshot. Availability means eligible for selection, not proven reachable. Active probes show whether any result has been observed. HTTP active_requests counts per-backend in-flight request ownership in every balancing mode. TCP has route-wide active connections and, for named members only, an instance-local count of established streams. Docker addresses are configured references, not resolved network scans. Capabilities describe this process, not remote fleet members.

get.summary: Read this instance's still-active retired backend generations (administrator only)
get.description: Returns only displaced HTTP/TCP generations with active admission leases, up to the bounded local registry capacity. HTTP admissions include in-flight work; TCP admissions include pending dials and established streams. Completed generations are pruned. This observation is instance-local and never proves fleet or drain completion. It does not expose an operator drain control.

get.summary: Read this instance's Docker connection (administrator only)
get.description: Returns server-side file path references for the local administrator, never certificate or private-key contents. This is instance-local state, not a fleet-wide setting. By default the private sidecar path appends `.docker-connection.json` to the full configuration filename; use `--docker-connection-state` to give each process a distinct path when multiple instances share a configuration file. An exclusive writer lock prevents accidental cross-process overwrite and is transferred during a same-version supervised hot restart. The supervisor binary must understand the DockerLock descriptor role before a later hot restart from this version. ETag is the quoted Docker connection revision, independent of route configuration revision.

put.summary: Set or disable this instance's Docker connection (administrator only)
put.description: If-Match must equal the quoted Docker connection revision. A disabled config overrides any CLI socket. This accepts local Unix sockets or certificate-verified HTTPS origins with server-side CA, client certificate, and private-key file references. It validates and persists the candidate before publication; use the test endpoint to verify daemon reachability.

delete.summary: Remove managed override and restore initial CLI socket fallback (administrator only)

post.summary: Verify a candidate Docker connection without activating it (administrator only)
post.description: Sends only GET /_ping to the Docker daemon with a three-second deadline and bounded response. Failure responses do not expose credential material.

get.summary: Read runtime status and current counters
Read signed updater state

post.summary: Request an immediate signed update check

get.summary: Read the complete active configuration

post.summary: Validate a configuration without changing runtime or persistent state

get.summary: List HTTP routes
Read an HTTP route
List TCP routes
Read a TCP route

post.description: Performs one inspect-only lookup when --docker-socket is configured. Routes may instead retain a docker://CONTAINER/NETWORK/PORT backend and use the periodic runtime discovery table.

post.summary: Hash a Basic authentication password into a credential line
post.description: Returns `username:salt_hex:sha256_hex` with a fresh 16-byte random salt for `basic_auth.credentials`. The password is hashed in memory and discarded; nothing is stored. Equivalent to `hangang --hash-password <user> <password>`.

get.summary: Check whether first-run administrator setup is required

post.description: Requires the existing HANGANG_ADMIN_TOKEN bearer credential. Creation is atomic and succeeds only while the local account store has no administrator; a later request returns 409. Account data is local to this instance.

post.summary: Sign in with an instance-local account
post.description: Returns an opaque eight-hour bearer session. Invalid credentials return a generic 401 response. No cookie is set.

get.summary: Read the current administrator or viewer identity
get.description: The existing break-glass bearer credential identifies as the system administrator.

post.description: The break-glass administrator bearer credential remains valid.

get.summary: Read local account audit recording policy
get.description: Administrator only. No-store. Returns the current ordered recording policy and cumulative filtered count for account create/update/delete. It does not configure HTTP or TCP traffic history.

200.description: Current local account audit recording policy

put.summary: Replace local account audit recording policy
put.description: Administrator only, no-store. Compare-and-swap expected_revision. A successful policy_change control receipt remains even when the policy drops account mutation records. A response failure or timeout is indeterminate; clients must refresh before deciding whether to submit another mutation.

200.description: Published local policy and new revision

get.summary: Read ordered local account audit records
get.description: Administrator-only ordered local account audit page. Live account authority is rechecked inside the read transaction. Account create/update/delete may be omitted by the current or previous recording policy; filtered_total and coverage_filtered disclose partial coverage. Baseline, bootstrap, retention and policy-change control receipts remain. Excludes login/logout, denied attempts, configuration recovery journals, HTTP/TCP history and other instances. No-store; pages are not a frozen multi-page export.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Exclusive sequence cursor; default0. pruned_through and truncated disclose unavailable earlier history.

200.description: A bounded ordered page and explicit retention coverage

post.summary: Explicitly prune local account audit through a sequence
post.description: Permanently removes records at or below through_id after a latest-sequence precondition and live administrator authorization. Removal, retention metadata and a new prune record commit atomically. The gateway does not prove records were exported; archive before pruning. No automatic retry on409. Available to recover audit capacity exhaustion.

200.description: Removed record count and newly committed prune event

get.summary: List instance-local management accounts
get.description: Administrator role required. Account-session authority is revalidated in the same SQLite read snapshot as the account list. Viewer or withdrawn authority receives 403; an initially invalid token receives 401; store failure receives 503.

post.description: Successful changes append a durable local account audit record atomically; audit capacity or storage failure returns 503 without a change. Administrator role is rechecked inside the account mutation transaction; a session revoked before that check returns 403 without changing accounts. Usernames must be unique; duplicate creation returns 409.

put.summary: Change role, enabled state, or password
put.description: Successful changes append a durable local account audit record atomically; audit capacity or storage failure returns 503 without a change. Administrator role is rechecked inside the account mutation transaction; a session revoked before that check returns 403 without changing accounts. The last enabled administrator cannot be demoted or disabled.

delete.description: Successful changes append a durable local account audit record atomically; audit capacity or storage failure returns 503 without a change. Administrator role is rechecked inside the account mutation transaction; a session revoked before that check returns 403 without changing accounts. The last enabled administrator cannot be deleted.

bearerAuth.description: Accepts the existing HANGANG_ADMIN_TOKEN break-glass credential or an opaque, eight-hour account session token returned by /v1/auth/login. Tokens are sent only in Authorization headers; no cookies are used.

observerAuth.description: Dedicated 48–256 character node-local observer token from the private dynamic file. It grants only GET /v1/fleet/observation and is never an administrator credential.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Quoted current revision of the resource being changed (route configuration or Docker connection).

LegacyError.description: Request rejected by a backward-compatible endpoint

observer_instance_id.description: Process-local collector identity; pair with generation when interpreting freshness across restarts or load-balanced admin endpoints.

fresh_nodes.description: Number of peers with a current fresh observation, including those reporting ready=false; not a count of healthy nodes.

endpoint.description: Validated HTTPS origin without path, query, fragment or userinfo; inventory only.

group_id.description: Unverified operator inventory label; null when omitted. No group or role authority is inferred.

role.description: Unverified operator inventory label; null when omitted. No group or role authority is inferred.

condition.description: Stale applies only after a previously fresh observation ages past 60 seconds; failures and identity mismatches remain explicit even when older.

observation.description: Historical last successful observation may remain visible during stale or unavailable conditions; only condition=fresh represents current freshness.

FleetCollectedObservation.description: Collector-validated local observation; store_epoch is null or 1..128 printable ASCII characters.

CountryObservation.description: Immutable copied observation at selected-route admission. Known requires country and digest; unknown requires digest without country/error; unavailable has an error, no country, and optional digest. Not-checked/not-configured contain no extra values. No file paths or database handles. A passive unavailable result does not itself deny requests.

CountryMetrics.description: Process-lifetime counters backed by the same fixed atomics as Prometheus. Known/unknown/unavailable count selected-route lookups. Allowed/denied/admission_unavailable count only enforced native country-policy decisions, not final response success. Concurrent reads are approximate, not a transactional sum. No IP, route or database-generation labels.

GeoIpStatus.description: A concurrent node-local observation. Pending configured slots can have ready false with null error/timestamp. Metadata can describe an expired loaded database with ready false; metadata presence alone is not readiness.

file.description: Normalized absolute UTF-8 node-local path; no NUL, dot or parent components. Provision the MMDB independently on each node.

GeoIpSource.description: Dynamic node-local GeoIP2-Country or GeoLite2-Country MMDB with IPv6 format (also supports IPv4). Configuration validation is structural; new runtime slots remain pending until post-publication file verification succeeds. Invalid reload removes availability. File size does not bound total verifier memory.

enabled.description: False retains the policy but disables redirects.

host.description: Lowercase exact DNS host without an IP literal, port or trailing dot. It must be an exact non-glob member of this route's host or hosts.

scheme.description: Fixed redirect destination scheme; the canonical host itself is not redirected. Use require_tls separately for HTTPS enforcement. http conflicts with a route that requires TLS.

path_prefixes.description: Included UTF-8 path prefixes. Each is at most 2,048 bytes and rejects query/fragment characters, backslashes, Unicode whitespace/control characters, and . or .. components. Matching is bytewise without percent decoding, at an exact or slash segment boundary.

exclude_path_prefixes.description: Excluded prefixes use the same grammar and take precedence. An exact prefix cannot occur in both lists. The combined UTF-8 bytes of both lists cannot exceed 65,536.

CanonicalDomainRedirect.description: Optional operator redirect policy for an HTTP route. Redirects use a fixed configured scheme and member host while preserving the original path and query. This policy does not share cookies, sessions, certificates, or application state between hosts. Host membership, cross-list overlap, combined UTF-8 byte limits and require_tls compatibility are enforced by the server; JSON Schema maxLength counts characters, not bytes.

CountryPolicy.description: Combined allow/deny length 1..256; known country deny wins. Nonempty allow requires on_unknown deny. Enforced policies require geoip_database. Unknown is a successful lookup without country, never a DB failure. HTTP country denial is 403; unavailable or invalid database/record is 503. TCP refuses before opening upstream. Enforcement occurs after route selection, before cache/Lua/origin. Enforced routes bypass response cache. Disabled policies remain structurally validated.

LanguagePolicy.description: Combined allow/deny length 1..32; case-insensitive duplicates within each list invalid. Deny wins. Empty/all-zero-quality present headers denied, missing follows on_missing. Malformed/oversized headers return 400; valid denied preference 403. Disabled policy remains structurally validated. See docs/LANGUAGE_POLICY.md.

SequencedReceiptPageResponse.description: Unsupported stores return empty receipts and null snapshot/next_after/has_more. A terminal empty page retains the requested cursor. No receipt total is inferred from the high-water: sequence gaps are valid.

operation_id.description: Canonical V2 sequence prefix and checksum; not a bearer credential.

writes_available.description: Receipt space and authority registration capacity for this query, not global readiness.

receipt.description: Historical commit only; same wire fields as current proof but different semantics.

writes_available.description: Receipt capacity only; not overall configuration-write readiness.

receipt_version.description: V1 random identity or V2 canonical authority/acceptance-sequence identity. Older servers may omit this field; console treats omission as explicitly labeled legacy V1 only.

release_state.description: Local observation of SQL V2 receipt pin release. Older servers may omit it; the console treats missing V2 state as protected and never prunes that row. Release is not SQL receipt deletion or fleet activation.

release_id.description: Stable durable release identity when allocated; null or absent before allocation.

socket_path.description: Absolute path to a local Docker Unix socket.

url.description: HTTPS origin only; no userinfo, path, query or fragment.

client_key_file.description: Absolute private process-owned client key path.

enabled.description: Configured, not proof that the Docker daemon is reachable.

max_bytes.description: Weighted entry capacity. Zero disables memory storage and requires disk configuration; this capacity is not a process RSS limit.

max_entries.description: Must be positive when max_bytes is nonzero.

directory.description: Absolute, dedicated, nonsymlinked per-instance directory. Hangang owns cache-v1.db inside it; a preexisting directory must be mode 0700 and an existing owned database mode 0600.

max_bytes.description: Physical SQLite main-file quota, rounded down to 4096-byte pages.

enabled.description: False retains cache settings but disables the cache runtime. Omitted when true.

max_object_bytes.description: Maximum weighted size of one key, status, headers and complete response body.

max_fills.description: Maximum concurrent cache fills. Capacity exhaustion bypasses caching.

fill_timeout_ms.description: Maximum time to capture one complete response for publication.

generation.description: Fleet-wide invalidation generation. Changing it (a fleet purge does this through the shared store) makes every instance drop its cached entries when it activates the revision.

RouteCache.description: ttl_seconds must be <= max_ttl_seconds. Response Cache-Control or Expires can shorten or extend the default only up to max_ttl_seconds. Keys partition exact request targets and end-to-end headers by route policy, client IP, and transport security.

generation.description: Invalidation generation the runtime currently enforces (from the configuration `cache.generation`).

scope.description: `instance`: only this process's tiers were cleared (file and controller modes). `fleet`: the shared configuration's `cache.generation` was raised through a CAS; every instance drops its entries when it activates the new revision.

generation.description: New generation (fleet scope); null when no cache is configured.

listener_id.description: default for the legacy public listener, otherwise the selected named listener ID.

server_time_unix_ms.description: Server clock for relative expiry display; do not use browser wall clock.

in_process_acme.description: Sanitized status of the in-process ACME runtime, if enabled; not an external issuer's state.

source.description: configured_file makes no claim about who issued the certificate.

fingerprint_sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the public leaf DER, not a private-key digest.

tls_binding.description: Configured means this instance enabled config TLS; it does not prove these disk bytes are currently served. Unknown includes inventory references on non-TLS instances.

renewal.description: Only a matching explicit issuer manifest supplies external renewal observation. renew_before_unix_ms is the eligibility threshold, not a guaranteed issuance time.

items.description: ASCII DNS name or a leading *. wildcard matching exactly one label. Hosts must be unique among enabled entries; inactive entries do not reserve names.

hosts.description: 1..128 SNI names normally; must be empty for the default certificate.

cert_file.description: Absolute path to a regular PEM certificate-chain file, limited to 1 MiB.

key_file.description: Absolute path to the matching regular PEM private-key file, limited to 1 MiB.

issuer_status_file.description: Optional explicit absolute normalized path to a private, process-owned hangang-acme-issuer status manifest. The inventory only attributes an issued certificate when the manifest matches its configured hosts, expiry and public leaf fingerprint. The field is a server-side path reference and is never returned by the inventory API.

default.description: Optional fallback for absent or unmatched SNI. At most one enabled default per set; requires empty hosts. Explicit SNI matches take precedence.

enabled.description: False retains this certificate entry in config but excludes its material from TLS loading and file watching. Re-enabling requires valid files. Omitted when true.

CertificateFiles.description: File references for one SNI certificate or explicit default fallback. Configuration never contains certificate or private-key PEM bytes.

cache.description: Global cache storage and fill limits. A route cache block also requires this setting.

certificates.description: File-backed SNI certificate set served when Hangang starts with --config-tls. The complete set is validated before publication and watched for atomic material reloads; ACME, manual TLS, and Kubernetes certificate authorities are mutually exclusive.

public_http.description: Ordered public HTTP/HTTPS listeners on this instance. IDs must be unique. The legacy CLI listener remains separately addressable as default. The complete document is validated and activated with the existing revisioned PUT /v1/config.

workload_http.description: Dedicated HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 mutual-TLS listeners. These are separate from ordinary public HTTP/HTTPS and ACME listeners. The complete set is atomically published with the configuration document.

cache_generation_floor.description: Highest cache invalidation generation ever committed in this document's history, maintained by the server (kept while `cache` is null). Writes that carry a lower `cache.generation` are raised to it, so re-enabling the cache or rolling the document back never reopens a namespace a purge retired.

listener_ids.description: Empty preserves legacy CLI listener scope. Nonempty selects exact public_http IDs or reserved default. Incompatible with workload_auth; dedicated workload mTLS listeners remain selected by workload_auth.listener_ids.

access_mode.description: Declared gateway authentication boundary. legacy is omitted on serialization and preserves existing behavior. protected requires basic_auth, jwt_auth, workload_auth or auth; JWT can compose with external authorization but cannot share Authorization with Basic. Workload authentication also requires resource_policy and an authorized dedicated HTTP mTLS listener. Protected routes bypass response caching. public and application forbid gateway authenticators; application means the upstream application owns authentication. Lua alone does not satisfy protected. A same-ID protected route cannot be replaced with omitted or legacy mode; explicitly choose public or application to downgrade. Validation applies even while the route is disabled.

resource_policy.description: Optional exact resource authorization. Requires protected access and a matching Basic, verified JWT, verified workload SPIFFE URI, or external authenticator even with enforce=false. An enforced resource namespace must first be saved with enforce=false before removal in a later revision, even if its route is renamed or disabled. Existing host aliases may be added or reordered without releasing protection; removal or path-scope changes require preservation of the old scope or prior explicit release. Reusing a resource ID requires the same policy and authenticators. External terminal_response is incompatible with any resource policy.

enabled.description: False retains the HTTP route and its rules but excludes it from new request matching, probes and discovery. Omitted when true.

cache.description: Enables shared response caching for this route when global cache storage is configured. Dynamic policy, request transforms, JSON body predicates, Lua response transforms, and streaming response transforms bypass caching.

host.description: Optional case-insensitive Host match. Supports DNS-label-local * and ? wildcards. Does not match across dots; conflicts with hosts and host_regex. Exact legacy host matching is retained.

hosts.description: Alternative case-insensitive Host patterns for a single route sharing its upstreams, policy, balancing and metrics. Matches when any alias matches. Supports the same label-local glob syntax as host; conflicts with host and host_regex. Duplicates are rejected case-insensitively. Omitted from serialized routes when empty. HTTP route priority and configuration order still decide between different routes.

canonical_domain.description: Optional canonical-host redirect policy for exact host or hosts routes.

path_prefix.description: Path operand interpreted by path_match. It must begin with /. Null disables path matching.

path_match.description: prefix uses byte-prefix matching; exact requires equality; segment_prefix matches the path itself or descendants separated by /. Ignored when path_prefix is null.

backends.description: Homogeneous legacy HTTP address strings or named pool members. Object members require local-file configuration authority in this release and balance.weights must be empty. Mixed arrays are rejected. Explicit conversion changes health identity.

max_requests.description: Optional per-route concurrent admission limit, retained across configuration revisions. Global admission limits also apply.

upstream_timeout_ms.description: Optional per-route time budget in milliseconds for the upstream to return response headers (covers request-body upload plus time-to-first-byte). Overrides the global --upstream-timeout-seconds default. Response body streaming afterwards is bounded by the transport idle timeout.

retries.description: Bounded retries to a freshly selected backend on a pre-response connection error, for safely replayable (bodyless idempotent, non-transform, non-upgrade) requests only.

require_tls.description: Redirect plaintext requests (by terminated transport or trusted X-Forwarded-Proto) to HTTPS using --https-redirect-code.

response_set_headers.description: Streaming-safe response header additions/replacements. Framing/hop-by-hop names are rejected.

realm.description: Challenge realm. Control characters, DEL, and a double quote are rejected.

items.description: Native username:salt_hex:sha256_hex, or migration-only v1:sha1-suffix:<base64url username>:<base64url suffix>:<40 hex digest>:<base64url identity JSON>. SHA-1 suffix format verifies SHA1(password || suffix), preserving a legacy credential without plaintext. Neither format is a memory-hard password KDF. Usernames must be unique; identity map keys are validated and cannot override framing/authority/credentials or external-auth identities.

credentials.description: Native credentials or versioned legacy compatibility credentials; generate new native entries with --hash-password.

accept_proxy_authorization.description: Compatibility mode: try Proxy-Authorization before Authorization. Proxy credentials are not forwarded upstream.

jwt_auth.description: Native RFC 9068 OAuth JWT access-token verification. A configured route validates every request before external authorization, Lua, and upstream forwarding. Basic authentication cannot coexist with JWT because both use Authorization. The Bearer token is removed before the upstream by default; if external authorization is configured it sees the token first. No OpenID Connect browser login or ID-token acceptance is implied.

workload_auth.description: Route-local verified workload identity admission from dedicated workload_http mTLS listeners. Requires protected access and a resource policy. Ordinary public listeners cannot satisfy it.

request_transform.description: Optional request body and header transformation. Native operations run before isolated Lua. See TRANSFORMS.md for streaming, HTTP semantics and bounds.

response_transform.description: Optional response body and header transformation. Native operations run before isolated Lua. See TRANSFORMS.md for streaming, HTTP semantics and bounds.

upstream_host.description: Override HTTP Host and HTTP/2 :authority without changing dial destination or TLS name. Conflicts with preserve_host.

preserve_host.description: Preserve incoming Host / :authority upstream. Conflicts with upstream_host.

priority.description: Higher priority matches first. Equal HTTP priorities retain configuration order; equal SNI priorities prefer exact names, simple suffix wildcards, general globs, then regexes.

host_regex.description: Whole-host ASCII regular expression, case-insensitive by default. Compiled before publication with 64 KiB compiled/DFA limits and nesting 32. No backreferences/lookaround. Conflicts with host; at most 256 host regexes across the configuration.

https_redirect_code.description: Per-route HTTPS requirement response code, overriding shared/process defaults.

language_policy.description: Selected-route Accept-Language admission before cache/Lua/origin; not identity or country proof. Routes sharing resource_id require the same policy.

request_headers.description: Client request headers copied to the authorization request. The generated context (x-forwarded-method/uri/proto/host/port/for, x-real-ip, x-original-url, x-original-method/uri/client-ip) is always added from the trusted-proxy resolution and cannot be listed here.

response_headers.description: Headers copied from an allowed auth response. Hop-by-hop and protected names are rejected; copied names and values have a 16 KiB aggregate limit.

forward_response.description: Forward a 3xx/401/403 authorization response (status, Location, Set-Cookie, WWW-Authenticate, Content-Type, Cache-Control) to the client for SSO redirect/cookie flows. The allowlisted forwarded header aggregate is limited to 16 KiB and the body to 64 KiB.

terminal_response.description: Opt-in: a configured authorization server may return a bounded terminal 2xx response with exactly one X-Hangang-Auth-Terminal: 1 header. The marker is never forwarded.

items.description: ASCII DNS name or label-local * / ? routing glob; wildcards never cross dots.

hosts.description: Exact DNS names or label-local * / ? glob patterns. Unknown SNI fails closed. At most 256 general SNI globs per listener; simple *.literal.suffix patterns use an indexed path.

host_regexes.description: Whole-host ASCII regular expressions, case-insensitive by default; compiled before publication. Combined hosts + host_regexes must contain 1..128 patterns, at most 8192 source bytes per route. Global host-regex limit 256.

SniMatch.description: Bounded TLS ClientHello inspection for TCP passthrough. Shared-listener inspection limits must agree. Higher priority wins; within a priority exact names precede simple suffix wildcards, general globs, then regexes. Identical patterns at the same priority are rejected; other overlaps use documented ordering.

cert_file.description: Absolute server certificate file path. PEM contents are not accepted through this field.

key_file.description: Absolute server private-key file path; the key is read by the runtime, never pasted into the API.

client_ca_file.description: Absolute trust-anchor file path for mandatory client-certificate verification.

client_crl_file.description: Optional absolute client certificate revocation-list file path.

allowed_uri_sans.description: Exact allowed SPIFFE URI SANs on the verified client certificate. The server enforces ASCII, lowercase trust domains, nonempty slash-separated path segments and a 2,048-byte limit. Userinfo, ports, percent escapes, query/fragment, dot segments and trailing slash are rejected. An absent match denies admission before the upstream dial.

handshake_timeout_ms.description: Bound for the inbound TLS client handshake.

TcpInboundTls.description: Dedicated TCP listener TLS termination with mandatory verified client certificate and exactly one allowlisted SPIFFE URI SAN. Cannot coexist with SNI passthrough. At most 64 distinct policies per configuration; material loads on enabled-route configuration publication. Disable or remove an active listener in a prior revision before removing authentication. Established streams check policy/material withdrawal and certificate/CRL expiry every 250 ms. Inbound authentication is separate from upstream TLS.

id.description: Stable public listener ID, unique across public_http; default is reserved for the legacy CLI listener.

listen.description: Nonzero IP socket address bound by this instance, for example 0.0.0.0:8080 or [::]:8443.

certificates.description: Empty serves plaintext HTTP; nonempty serves HTTPS using this listener's file-backed SNI set. Certificate paths resolve on each instance. The combined input bytes of all certificate and key PEM files for one named listener are limited to 1 MiB; at most 1,024 certificate entries may be configured across all named public listeners. This is separate from the legacy global certificate set limit.

trusted_proxy_cidrs.description: Only peers in this explicit list may supply forwarding headers. Empty means none; this does not inherit settings.trusted_proxy_cidrs.

id.description: Stable listener ID referenced by HTTP route workload_auth.listener_ids.

listen.description: Dedicated nonzero IP socket address, separate from ordinary public HTTP/HTTPS listeners.

enabled.description: False retains the listener policy without binding or accepting new connections. Omission means true.

tls.description: Server material, mandatory client CA/optional CRL, and listener-level exact SPIFFE URI SAN allowlist.

listener_ids.description: Exact IDs of dedicated workload_http listeners admitted by this route. A configured but disabled or unavailable listener is never accepted until it becomes active.

allowed_uri_sans.description: Route-local exact authorized SPIFFE URI SANs. The verified client URI must also be in the selected listener's TLS allowlist and satisfy the resource policy.

identity_header.description: Optional upstream request header set only from the verified SPIFFE URI. Client and Lua values cannot establish it.

WorkloadAuth.description: Requires Protected access_mode and resource_policy. Authentication from the selected dedicated HTTP mTLS listener composes conjunctively with Basic, JWT and external authorization when configured. An ordinary public HTTP/HTTPS listener cannot provide this identity.

enabled.description: False retains the TCP route but does not bind its listener or admit new connections. Omitted when true.

sni.description: Optional SNI passthrough match. A listener cannot mix SNI and non-SNI routes.

inbound_tls.description: Optional inbound mutual TLS termination and SPIFFE client identity check. Cannot be combined with SNI passthrough; null or absent preserves raw TCP.

listen.description: IP socket address with a nonzero port.

backends.description: Homogeneous legacy TCP address strings or named pool members. Object members require local-file configuration authority in this release. Mixed arrays are rejected. Explicit conversion changes health identity.

max_connections.description: Optional per-route concurrent admission limit, retained across configuration revisions. Global admission limits also apply.

health.description: Optional transport-level TCP connection probes. Absent/null disables probes; these do not verify application health.

priority.description: Higher priority matches first. Equal HTTP priorities retain configuration order; equal SNI priorities prefer exact names, simple suffix wildcards, general globs, then regexes.

docker_enabled.description: A Docker resolver is configured in this process.

self_restart_enabled.description: This process has a supervisor control channel.

signed_updates_enabled.description: A signed update manifest and supervisor control channel are configured.

member_id.description: Stable configured ID for an object-mode pool member; null for legacy string targets. Index remains display order only.

address.description: Configured target, possibly a Docker reference; no network lookup is performed.

match_host.description: Configured HTTP host pattern, group: prefix with comma-separated aliases, or regex: prefix for a host regex; null for unrestricted HTTP and TCP.

listen.description: TCP route listener; null for HTTP.

enabled.description: Configured route activation state. False retains the row but excludes its route from new traffic.

available.description: Eligible according to route activation, member gate, local health and current Docker discovery evidence. Not a reachability or health guarantee.

desired_state.description: Configured state of this target; legacy string targets report serving. Draining blocks new admissions while existing work continues. Maintenance additionally stops probes.

admission_open.description: Current member admission gate only; route activation and health eligibility are separate. This is not a reachability test or fleet-wide state.

active_admissions.description: Instance-local leases on this current member generation. TCP includes pending dials and established streams; HTTP includes in-flight work. Displaced retired generations are reported separately by /v1/retired-members. Zero does not prove fleet drain completion.

probe_observed.description: Whether an HTTP active probe or TCP connection probe result has been recorded; null without active probing.

initial_check_pending.description: True while a checking-startup backend has not met its healthy HTTP or TCP connection probe threshold; false after release or with healthy-default startup; null without active health checks.

active_requests.description: HTTP per-backend live request ownership count in every balancing mode. Always null for TCP.

member_active_streams.description: Named TCP members only: instance-local established stream count for the continuously present (route ID, member ID) identity. Includes old endpoint generations across address, health, or route enablement changes; excludes pending dials. Null for HTTP and legacy TCP. Rename or removal followed by re-addition starts fresh identity. This count alone never proves drain completion.

route_active_connections.description: TCP route-wide admission count repeated for its target rows; not per-backend load. Null for HTTP.

retirement_id.description: Instance-local unsigned 64-bit retirement identifier; not a cross-instance generation key.

member_id.description: Named member ID, or null for a legacy string target.

address.description: Configured address of the retired backend generation.

active_admissions.description: HTTP in-flight work or TCP pending dials and established streams still held by this retired generation. A row may reach zero while being serialized and will be pruned later.

TcpDecimal.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer encoded as canonical decimal text so browsers retain precision. The schema enforces decimal shape and length; clients must also check the u64 range.

peer_ip.description: Canonical accepted socket peer address; TCP does not trust forwarding headers.

event_id.description: Completion-order event cursor, independent of connection accept ID.

policy_revision.description: Configuration revision whose TCP recent-recording policy selected this completion. Null only for standalone history without a policy provider.

process_id.description: Instance process generation; reset cursors when this changes.

active_untracked.description: Current connections beyond tracking capacity; never blocks the data plane.

best_effort.description: Multi-page active reads are not a frozen inventory.

process_id.description: Instance process generation; reset cursors when this changes.

gap.description: Requested cursor precedes retained events or belongs to a newer process generation.

filtered_total.description: Instance-lifetime completions intentionally omitted by settings.tcp_recent_recording. Separate from dropped_total (retention/ring eviction) and omitted_total (untracked active capacity).

TrafficListener.description: Accepted HTTP listener from server-side connection evidence. Never derived from client headers. Unknown indicates absent trusted transport information.

id.description: default for a known CLI listener, a configured ID for public or workload, or null only when kind is unknown.

policy_revision.description: Configuration revision whose HTTP recording policy decided whether this response-head metadata was recorded. This is not a durable audit sequence; JSON u64 consumers must preserve numeric precision.

path.description: Path only; query string and raw Host are discarded. Display truncates to 256 characters; policy matching uses the full URI path.

filtered_total.description: Instance-lifetime cumulative HTTP response-head records intentionally omitted by settings.http_recording. Separate from dropped_total, which counts ring eviction/TTL. Never infer complete history from a zero value if this field is absent on an older server; JSON u64 consumers must preserve numeric precision.

server_time_unix_ms.description: Server snapshot time in Unix milliseconds, used with record timestamps to compute remaining retention without trusting the browser clock.

gap.description: True if the supplied cursor was older than retained entries or newer than this process generation.

id.description: Configured TCP route ID or dedicated HTTP workload listener ID.

ready.description: True only when this instance has a verified current material generation for the enabled binding. False means authenticated admission is closed.

workload_materials.description: This instance's enabled TCP and dedicated HTTP workload mTLS bindings only. Ready means a verified local material generation is available; false closes authenticated admission. No paths, certificates, or private keys are returned. This is local runtime state, not fleet readiness.

store.description: Shared configuration store diagnostics; null in file and controller modes.

settings.description: Legacy active runtime settings summary (empty object when none are set). HTTP recording rules are omitted because this response is viewer-readable; administrators read them through GET /v1/config.

policy_errors_total.description: Historical aggregate of route Lua policy failures, including local worker capacity rejections.

policy_capacity_rejections_total.description: Subset of policy_errors_total caused by route Lua worker capacity being busy or restarting. Does not include body transforms.

jwt_auth_rejections_total.description: Native JWT invalid-token 401 plus JWT required scope/group permission 403. Does not include the separate resource-policy exact subject/method denial.

jwt_auth_unavailable_total.description: Native JWT key acquisition or verifier infrastructure unavailable, returned as 503.

jwt_lease_terminations_total.description: Admitted JWT request/body/tunnel guards terminated after token time invalidation, signing-key withdrawal or same-route generation retirement. Operational guard count, not unique users or durable audit.

jwt_auth_capacity_rejections_total.description: Native JWT cryptographic admission limit reached, returned as 503.

tcp_mtls_rejections_total.description: Inbound TCP mutual-TLS handshake, client URI SAN, or current-generation admission rejection.

tcp_mtls_lease_terminations_total.description: Authenticated TCP streams terminated after certificate or CRL expiry or withdrawal of their prepared policy generation. Unrelated configuration changes preserve an unchanged prepared policy.

http_mtls_rejections_total.description: Dedicated HTTP mTLS listener client handshake or listener-generation admission rejections.

http_mtls_lease_terminations_total.description: Authenticated dedicated HTTP listener connections terminated after certificate/CRL expiry or prepared listener policy withdrawal.

workload_auth_rejections_total.description: HTTP route workload identity authorization denials after listener authentication. Distinct from resource-policy subject/method denials.

workload_route_terminations_total.description: Authenticated HTTP route streams terminated when the accepted route policy generation is withdrawn.

DockerBackendReference.description: Dynamic Docker backend in the exact form docker://CONTAINER/NETWORK/PORT. Names are 1..128 ASCII alphanumeric, dot, underscore, or hyphen characters and begin alphanumeric; the canonical decimal port is 1..65535.

HttpBackend.description: A native HTTP(S) upstream URL without credentials or query, or a Docker discovery reference.

TcpBackend.description: A native host:port authority or a Docker discovery reference.

id.description: Stable, byte-exact ID unique within this route. Renaming changes member health identity.

desired_state.description: Serving accepts new local admissions. Draining blocks new admissions but keeps existing work. Maintenance also stops health probes. No deadline or force-close is implied.

HttpPoolMember.description: Named HTTP pool member. IDs and addresses must each be unique in the route. Object-mode routes cannot use legacy balance.weights.

id.description: Stable, byte-exact ID unique within this route. Renaming changes member health identity.

desired_state.description: Serving accepts new local admissions. Draining blocks new admissions but keeps existing work. Maintenance also stops health probes. No deadline or force-close is implied.

TcpPoolMember.description: Named TCP pool member with a per-member weight. IDs and addresses must each be unique in the route. Legacy TCP string routes remain equal weight.

resource_id.description: Opaque ASCII namespace ID. Same ID across routes requires the same policy and authenticator.

enforce.description: False keeps the policy configured but disables namespace and subject enforcement. Gateway authentication still runs, and all schema/authenticator checks still apply.

allow.description: Exact allowlist; an empty array denies all requests while enforced. Aggregate subject/method entries and text are bounded by the server.

subject_header.description: Exact header configured in auth.response_headers and copied only from a successful external authorization response. Comma-ambiguous subjects are denied.

oneOf.description: The sub claim of an RFC 9068 access token verified using this route's jwt_auth issuer, audience and signing keys. Client headers and Lua cannot establish it.
The exact canonical SPIFFE URI SAN from a verified client certificate on an allowed dedicated HTTP mTLS listener. Client headers and Lua cannot establish it; subjects may be up to 2,048 ASCII bytes.

hide_credentials.description: Remove the verified Bearer token before forwarding to the upstream. If external authorization is configured, it is called before this removal.

identity_header.description: Optional upstream request header containing only the verified JWT sub. Authorization, Host, framing, forwarding, cookie and WebSocket protocol names are forbidden. Clients, Lua and native transforms cannot replace its authenticated value.

issuer.description: Exact HTTPS issuer URL with no credentials, query or fragment. The signed iss claim must match exactly.

audiences.description: Configured resource audiences; signed aud must contain one. Item length is bounded in UTF-8 bytes by the server.

profile.description: Only signed OAuth access tokens with at+jwt or application/at+jwt typ are accepted; OIDC ID tokens are rejected.

algorithms.description: Explicit asymmetric signing algorithms. The token algorithm and JWK key type must agree; HS and none are never accepted.

scope_claim.description: Distinct nonregistered claim name for space-delimited OAuth scopes.

groups_claim.description: Distinct nonregistered claim name for a group string array.

required_scopes.description: All exact scopes listed here are required. A valid signed token missing one receives 403.

required_groups.description: All exact groups listed here are required. A valid signed token missing one receives 403.

revocation.description: Optional operator-managed revocation conditions for this route issuer. Published changes retire existing streams on the whole edited route. No online issuer logout or cross-node acknowledgement is implied.

issued_before.description: Reject signed iat strictly before this UNIX-second cutoff; equality is accepted. Token leeway does not relax this condition. Omit or null for no issuance cutoff.

token_ids.description: Exact signed jti values to reject with 401. Each is 1–255 UTF-8 bytes without surrounding whitespace or controls. Token identifiers only; do not supply bearer tokens. Stored with configuration, with no automatic expiry or deletion.

JwtRevocation.description: Bounded route-scoped policy, compiled before publication. Either condition denies admission. Removing an entry or lowering a cutoff can reallow a still-valid token; old closed streams do not resume. Shared-resource aliases must use the same complete JWT policy.

oneOf.description: Operator-configured local public JWK Set, compiled for this route. No private key parameters or token-selected URLs.
Bounded HTTPS OIDC discovery or explicit JWKS URL configured by the operator. An unknown key never determines a URL.

items.description: Public JWK with a globally unique bounded kid. Compatible signing keys use algorithm-matched kty, crv/use/key_ops; bounded public encryption or other-algorithm entries may be skipped. At least one usable signing key is required. Private JWK members are rejected by server validation.

JwtPublicJwks.description: At most 128 KiB serialized. Duplicate JSON member names, private parameters, ambiguous key IDs and weak key material are rejected by the server.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Hard freshness limit measured from fetch start. Known keys trigger an inline early refresh after half the TTL, subject to cooldown; peers can use still-fresh keys. Failures never extend the deadline, and expired keys cannot authorize.

refresh_cooldown_seconds.description: At most the cache TTL. Unknown kid refreshes are singleflight and rate-limited.

ca_pem.description: Optional additional public CA certificate. Private key material is rejected.

oneOf.description: Fetch OIDC configuration from the exact configured issuer, validate discovered issuer exactly, then fetch its same-origin HTTPS jwks_uri. Pin an explicit JWKS endpoint to trust another origin.
Explicit operator-configured HTTPS JWKS URL without credentials, query or fragment.

items.description: Exact subject with no wildcard semantics. Basic, JWT and external subjects are 1–255 UTF-8 bytes without surrounding whitespace or controls; workload subjects are canonical SPIFFE URIs up to 2,048 ASCII bytes.

methods.description: Uppercase ASCII letters, digits or hyphen, or a sole * entry meaning every method.

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed admitted operations before temporary quarantine.

BalanceConfig.description: HTTP admission balancing. Requests are never replayed. Weights apply to round-robin admission and as relative capacity for least-connections.

weights.description: Legacy string backends only: empty means weight 1 for every backend; otherwise the array length must equal the backend count. Named object members use their own weight and require this array empty.

health.description: Optional passive health quarantine based on observed connection/request success.

phase.description: Disabled (empty), pending, ready, issuing, retrying or configuration-error. Credentials are never exposed.

mode.description: Whole body; LF/CRLF lines; one JSON value per line; or SSE events with CR/LF/CRLF framing. Streaming modes retain only a bounded record.

lua.description: UTF-8 source limited to 16 KiB in bytes. Runs in a fresh isolated VM per body/record. When present, max_buffer_bytes and max_output_bytes must both be explicitly <=16384.

timeout_ms.description: Buffered read and transformation deadline; streaming deadline per complete record. Lua also has independent worker deadlines.

set_headers.description: Replace all values for a name. Framing, routing identity, encoding, range and validator headers are forbidden.

BodyTransform.description: At most 32 combined header mutations and 64 KiB of operation/header/script configuration. JSON and XML operations cannot mix. Runtime caps also cover intermediate representations. Encoded bodies, tunnels, ranges and preconditions have explicit restrictions; see transformation guide.

BodyOperation.description: Ordered native operations. JSON uses RFC 6901 pointers with existing parents/array indices. XML uses exact ASCII qualified-name paths, not XPath; set_text replaces all descendants and remove removes matching subtrees. Root removal is forbidden.

OutboundOptions.description: Route-specific outbound connection policy. Applies only to selected route traffic, not external authorization, ACME or control-plane requests. unix_socket is exclusive with connect_address, socks5, and dns_servers; TLS remains optional.

connect_address.description: host:port or [IPv6]:port to dial; does not change Host or TLS SNI.

unix_socket.description: Absolute normalized Unix socket path inside the gateway, at most 107 encoded bytes. Dials the socket instead of TCP while the logical backend supplies Host and TLS SNI/name. Exclusive with connect_address, socks5 and dns_servers. The socket must be mounted and protected separately.

dns_servers.description: Explicit IP:port DNS servers (UDP with TCP fallback); empty uses system DNS for direct connections or remote DNS for SOCKS5. With SOCKS5, selected DNS resolves target locally before sending IP. No fallback to system DNS.

address.description: SOCKS5 CONNECT proxy host:port. No direct fallback on error.

username_env.description: Environment variable name; must be paired with password_env. Never embed credentials.

password_env.description: Environment variable name; value is never returned by the API.

UpstreamTls.description: Enables TLS wrapping for TCP routes; requires HTTPS backends for HTTP routes. Settings apply only to upstream connections.

server_name.description: TLS verification name and SNI, independent of dial address and HTTP Host; defaults to logical backend name.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Explicitly skips server certificate chain/name verification for this route. TLS remains encrypted and handshake signatures are checked, but server identity is not authenticated.

ca_file.description: Absolute local regular PEM CA file, max 1 MiB. Loaded before configuration publication; at most 16 routes may use CA files. Conflicts with insecure_skip_verify.

max_fragment_size.description: Optional rustls TLS record size limit, including record header for unencrypted ClientHello. Applies to all outgoing records, not only SNI. Does not control TCP packet boundaries or guarantee censorship bypass.

id.description: Random per-process identifier, so instances behind one load-balanced address can be told apart.

config_digest.description: Digest of the active configuration document excluding its revision; members at one revision must agree.

epoch.description: Authority epoch this instance follows (32 hex chars); null until the first successful poll.

degraded.description: A transport-class failure (unavailable, missing, indeterminate, stalled) is being tolerated inside the grace window.

reason.description: Current failure class; null when the last poll confirmed agreement.

grace_seconds.description: `--store-grace-seconds`: how long transport-class failures are tolerated before readiness is withdrawn.

items.description: Exact SocketAddr captured from an accepting raw TCP socket. The address may remain after its route is removed or moved, so a held stream can still match at completion. This field does not select workload HTTP listeners.
IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR; IPv4-mapped IPv6 accepted peers are canonicalized to IPv4.

route_matched.description: When false, route_ids must be empty.

TcpRecentRecordingMatch.description: Populated fields combine with AND; alternatives within each array combine with OR. Empty match selects all raw TCP completions. No country, SNI, forwarded-header or payload predicates.

TcpRecentRecordingRule.description: IDs are unique within a policy. Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins.

TcpRecentRecordingPolicy.description: Optional settings.tcp_recent_recording policy, at most 64 KiB serialized. Missing policy records all completions. Selection occurs at completion using the current published policy and revision. Existing rows remain until retention expiry. Active TCP tracking, aggregate counters, admission and routing are unchanged.

HttpRecordingStatusRange.description: Inclusive HTTP status range; min must be at most max.

route_matched.description: When false, route_ids must be empty.

items.description: ASCII graphic raw URI path prefix, with no query or fragment; matched against the full path before ring display truncation.
IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR network parsed by ipnet.
IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR network parsed by ipnet; client IP follows configured trusted-proxy boundary.

HttpRecordingMatch.description: Populated fields combine with AND, array alternatives with OR; missing/empty fields are unrestricted. Empty match selects every completed HTTP response-head event.

HttpRecordingRule.description: IDs must be unique in a policy. Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins.

HttpRecordingPolicy.description: Optional settings.http_recording policy (serialized at most 64 KiB). It selects completed HTTP response-head metadata for the bounded ring and optional CLI access trace. Missing policy records by default. It never changes admission, routing, authentication, aggregate metrics, durable account audit, SQL receipts or TCP history. Health probes are excluded. Existing ring rows remain until retention expiry, and intentional omission counts do not reset on policy changes.

Settings.description: Process-wide runtime settings carried in the document so every instance of a fleet converges on them. A present field overrides the command-line value of the same name; an absent field keeps the process default. Applied on the next request after activation.

trusted_proxy_cidrs.description: Peers whose X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Port are trusted (overrides --trusted-proxy-cidrs).

remove_response_headers.description: Response headers removed from every upstream response (overrides --remove-response-headers). Protected framing headers are rejected.

upstream_timeout_ms.description: Default upstream response-header timeout for routes without upstream_timeout_ms (overrides --upstream-timeout-seconds).

allow_dot_segments.description: Accept request paths containing dot segments (overrides --allow-dot-segments).

health_path.description: Unauthenticated readiness probe path on the public listener (overrides --health-path).

username.description: No colon, no surrounding whitespace, no control characters.

interval_ms.description: Milliseconds between per-backend TCP connection probes.

timeout_ms.description: Connection-probe deadline; must not exceed interval_ms.

healthy_successes.description: Consecutive successful probes needed to release checking startup or recover an excluded backend.

unhealthy_failures.description: Consecutive failed connection probes before excluding a backend.

initial_state.description: Omitted/healthy preserves immediately eligible startup. Checking withholds each backend until healthy_successes successful connection probes.

TcpHealthPolicy.description: Transport-level probes use the configured outbound DNS, SOCKS5 and TLS handshake, then close without sending application bytes. Success is connection reachability, not application health. At most 1024 probed TCP backends across the configuration.

initial_state.description: Optional startup admission state. Omitted/healthy preserves existing behavior: initially selectable until health observations exclude it. Checking starts every backend unavailable until healthy_successes consecutive successful active probes; failures, timeouts, and passive reports cannot release the initial gate.

path.description: Printable absolute origin path for GET probes, without query or fragment.

host.description: Bare printable host, without a port or user information.

ActiveHealthPolicy.description: Bounded GET probes using the route outbound policy. Probe targets support http://, https:// and discovered docker:// backends. Timeout must not exceed interval. At most 1024 probed backends across the configuration. Healthy/unhealthy status sets must not overlap. Optional initial_state=checking withholds each backend from selection until its healthy-success threshold is met; Docker endpoint replacement resets health evidence and fences stale probe and passive results by discovery epoch.

PassiveHealthPolicy.description: Passive quarantine with dedicated HTTP/transport/timeout thresholds. Requires active health for recovery and conflicts with legacy cooldown health. Healthy passive responses do not reset failure counters or recover a backend; successful active probes clear passive quarantine.

AccountAuditPolicyMatch.description: Fields combine with AND; values within a field combine with OR. Missing or empty arrays are unrestricted. An empty match explicitly matches all account create/update/delete events.

AccountAuditPolicyRule.description: Rule IDs must be unique within the policy; rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins.

AccountAuditPolicy.description: Local account create/update/delete recording only. Baseline, bootstrap, audit pruning, configuration-operation pruning and policy-change control receipts always remain. Configuration operation and SQL recovery evidence are independent.

through_id.description: For prune this is an account-audit sequence boundary; for config_operations_prune it is a configuration-operation sequence boundary.

policy_snapshot.description: Present only on policy_change control receipts; other actions omit it.

UserAuditRecord.description: No usernames, passwords, bearer tokens, hashes or raw bodies. baseline declares observation start, not historical events. IDs remain ordered/non-reused after migration and retention pruning. policy_revision is 0 for legacy records; a policy_change receipt contains the published policy snapshot.

writes_available.description: Whether the observed row count leaves audit capacity for another account mutation. This is not a guarantee of future disk or transaction success.

coverage_filtered.description: True when the recording policy has omitted account mutation events at any time in retained accounting; the audit is partial even when rows remain ordered.

token.description: Opaque bearer session; keep only in tab memory.
